question: Drug of choice for relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Beta IFN" -> "modulates immune response" -> "reduces inflammation" -> "decreases relapse rate" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Natalizumab" -> "blocks immune cell migration" -> "prevents CNS inflammation" -> "reduces relapse frequency" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Gamma IFN" -> "possible immune modulation" -> "unclear effect on MS" -> "potential worsening of symptoms" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Alpha IEN" -> "unclear mechanism in MS" -> "no established benefit" -> "not recommended for MS" -> 30%
analysis: Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) is commonly treated with disease-modifying therapies that aim to reduce the frequency and severity of relapses. Beta Interferon (Beta IFN) is widely recognized as a first-line treatment for RRMS due to its ability to modulate the immune system and decrease relapse rates. Natalizumab is another effective treatment for RRMS, but it is typically reserved for patients who do not respond adequately to first-line therapies like Beta IFN or have more aggressive disease. Gamma Interferon is not used in MS treatment as it can exacerbate the condition, and Alpha IEN is not a recognized treatment for MS. Based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, Beta IFN is the most appropriate first-line treatment for RRMS.
